This *may* end up changing casting behavior in very subtle ways, we'll need to run some internal tests to see if it causes problems or not. (@qlzh727 as a heads up)

Okay, I've checked the comprehensive internal google tests of Keras users. This causes around ~100 internal test failures.

This is because the Keras add layer (which is built on the Keras merge layer) and the `+` tensor operator have fundamentally different behaviors.

There appear to be at least two main differences (though possibly more):
1. Supported shapes:
The Keras add layer will only add tensors of the exact same shape. The tensor `+` operator will broadcast scalars/tensors w/ fewer dimensions.

E.g.
```
tf.ones(shape=(3, 4)) + 2.0
```
Outputs:
```
<tf.Tensor: shape=(3, 4), dtype=float32, numpy=
array([[3., 3., 3., 3.],
       [3., 3., 3., 3.],
       [3., 3., 3., 3.]], dtype=float32)>
```

While:
```
tf.keras.layers.Add()([tf.ones(shape=(3, 4)), 2.0])
```
Raises:
```
InvalidArgumentError: Tried to expand dim index 1 for tensor with 0 dimensions. [Op:ExpandDims]
```

2. The Keras layer introduces autocasting semantics.
E.g. adding two float64 tensors directly outputs a float64 tensor:
```
tf.ones(shape=(3, 4), dtype=tf.float64) + tf.ones(shape=(3, 4), dtype=tf.float64)
```
```
<tf.Tensor: shape=(3, 4), dtype=float64, numpy=
array([[2., 2., 2., 2.],
       [2., 2., 2., 2.],
       [2., 2., 2., 2.]])>
```

But using the add layer autocasts to a float32 tensor:
```
tf.keras.layers.Add()([tf.ones(shape=(3, 4), dtype=tf.float64), tf.ones(shape=(3, 4), dtype=tf.float64)])
```

```
<tf.Tensor: shape=(3, 4), dtype=float32, numpy=
array([[2., 2., 2., 2.],
       [2., 2., 2., 2.],
       [2., 2., 2., 2.]], dtype=float32)>
```

----------------------
All in all, this change breaks backwards compatibility and I don't think is worth the slightly-nicer model representation it would provide (of an Add layer instead of a tf.__add__ tfoplayer)

Perhaps we can revisit the semantics of `Add` layers in the future and make them more consistent with the `+` binary operator. At that point we could apply this change.

@anerirana if you're still interested in contributing something around this, perhaps you could contribute unit tests that mean we wouldn't have to run the full internal tests if we ever did want to revisit applying this change?

(e.g. use the above examples that work for `+` but not `layers.Add`
@tomerk, thanks for the review. Yes, I will go ahead and add the unit tests pertaining to the above-mentioned differences.

issue_context.title: Overriding `__add__` on `KerasTensor` class
issue_context.body:
When doing `z = x + y` with KerasTensors, right now, the generate node in the Functional graph is a TFOpLayer wrapping `tf.add`. Instead, it would be nicer if the generated node was a Keras `Add` layer. This would keep the graph more readable and would simplify serialization.

Like this:

```
from tensorflow import keras
x = keras.Input(shape=(1,))
y = keras.Input(shape=(1,))
z = x + y
model = keras.Model([x, y], z)
model.summary()
```

This can be achieved by overriding `__add__` on the KerasTensor class. Likewise we should do this for other operators when possible.
comments: Hi @fchollet, unless I'm missing something, will referencing the Keras Add layer on the KerasTensor class cause a circular import? Do you think we should make the changes in the Functional class instead? Thanks
